listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Tuesday, November 24. Our lead story is about Nvidia. President Trump says he convinced the company to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive. BBC World reports that the claim has drawn backlash. Nvidia had come under pressure from Trump to reappoint Huang. The BBC says Huang's comeback helped add one trillion dollars to the company's stock value. Now for the front page. Anthropic has announced that Claude Opus 4.5 will be retired on the Claude API on January 22, 2027. The company recommends moving to Claude Opus 5.5. In basketball, Kevin Durant scored 32 points as the Houston Rockets beat the Los Angeles Clippers 116 to 104. Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each added 20. In architecture, Buro Happold and Motif are working to connect AI-driven design with deterministic computation, to change how architects and engineers collaborate in BIM. And in Atlanta, the city zoning committee unanimously denied a request for a 225-foot luxury condo tower in Old Fourth Ward. Neighbors had contested the project. Now the sections. In tech, Anthropic launched Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in beta, which offers zero data retention for eligible organizations. In politics, The Lever reports that Democrats' plan to investigate Nvidia could collide with a billionaire donor on the company's board. Also, Oregon and Virginia are suing Elon Musk's AI company over sexualized deepfakes made with Grok. In world news, NPR reports that fighting between Russia and Ukraine has expanded geographically. A Russian warship was sunk in a Libyan port, and Russian missiles landed in Poland. In sports, the Seahawks plan to start Sam Darnold against the 49ers but will check on him in Wednesday's practice. The 49ers also released receiver Brandon Aiyuk, and agreed to an extension with general manager John Lynch. In Atlanta, the Gemini project near the Beltline in Reynoldstown has started topping out. In architecture, a BIM Pure interview explains the vision behind Motif, an agentic BIM modeling app. In science, Science News reports that a human mathematician working with AI has apparently settled the Riemann hypothesis, a puzzle that is 167 years old. NASA is also seeking partners to design a nuclear reactor for the Moon. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
lead.note: President Trump says he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, and the claim has drawn backlash, according to BBC World. The company had come under pressure from Trump to reappoint Huang. The BBC reports that Huang's comeback helped add $1tn to Nvidia's stock value. That figure is the clearest sign of how much the market cared about the decision. The story sits where politics, a major company and the AI industry meet, which is why it is worth a reader's attention today. The summary does not say how the decision was reached, so the account rests on what Trump has said and on the reaction to it. Other outlets in today's feed are also covering the return, and the Politics section has a related story on Democratic plans to investigate Trump's dealings with Nvidia.
